title: The Circuit: An Immersive Silent Disco Ballet in Dumbo presented by N...
transcript: In the heart of Dumbo, Brooklyn is a hyper-inventive theatrical experience called The Circuit. Billed as “an immersive silent disco ballet,” it's an outdoor experience that's part dance show and part walking tour of a remarkably picturesque neighborhood. With a pulsing score and a low-overhead lighting design that moves with the dancers throughout the built in set design of the streets of New York, it leads you through a loose narrative about the ephemerality and cyclical nature of party culture. The title of the piece is clever in its double meaning. While it's primarily a dance piece, there is a script overlaying the score that functions as dialogue and sometimes as internal thoughts. The intimacy through which the sound is delivered via the personal headset definitely contributes to the immersive nature of the performance and helps keep you from getting distracted by all the activity inevitably happening outside of the performance. As far as what I thought of the piece, the storytelling felt pretty gestural, but that's like most ballets I've attended. The experience itself was quite memorable, and it was a really lovely way to spend a breezy summer evening in Brooklyn. If this sounds up your alley, The Circuit is running through Labor Day weekend.
